rootCause.description: When skipError fires it pops a symbol off the parse stack but orphans #semantic-action items sitting below it. Those actions still fire later but their expected AST nodes were never pushed. make*SubTree functions then pop garbage/stale pointers and segfault.
rootCause.triggerInput: example-bubblesort.src with '=' instead of ':=' (wrong assignment operator)
rootCause.crashSite: makeBinarySubTreeWithHead in src/parser.cpp — called for 'whilestatement', pops 3 nodes, one or more are stale pointers

parseStackAtCrash: #assign <- orphaned, never fires or fires on wrong token
<expr>  <- expands but with wrong current token
#reptstatement4 <- pops 3 nodes: assign leaf + lhs + rhs, one is corrupt

attempts.name: Drain adjacent #actions inside skipError
attempts.description: After each pop in skipError, while-loop peeks at parsingStack.top(); if it starts with '#', pops it and pushes an epsilonNode placeholder onto the semantic stack.
attempts.reason: Only catches actions immediately adjacent to the skipped terminal. Actions for deeply nested rules (whilestatement pops condition + blocks each built from sub-actions) were still orphaned. The drain only fired for #statement one level up.

attempts.name: parseError flag on semanticActions, guard every make* function
attempts.description: Added 'bool parseError = false' to semanticActions in parser.h. Set it in skipError on every error. Added early-exit guards at top of makeLeaf, makeBinarySubTreeWithHead, makeBinarySubTree, makeSubTree, passAlong (both overloads). Each guard pops expected N items and pushes one epsilonNode placeholder instead.

subAttempts.reason: Nodes still referenced via sibling/parent pointers set during earlier normal-mode operations. Deleting them caused use-after-free crashes.

reasons: parseError trips on ANY minor error including ones skipError handles without corrupting the stack. Even correct bubblesort.src crashed (exit -1073741819) because some minor error set the flag.
passAlong('start') in error mode set astPtr->treeHead = nullptr, causing null dereference later in the driver when it tried to traverse the tree.

nextSteps.description: Only set parseError when skipError is called during a rule mid-way through building a semantic subtree. Check if parsingStack has pending '#' items below the skipped symbol before setting the flag — not on all errors.
In passAlong error mode, push epsilon onto the semantic stack even for nodeType='start'. Do not set treeHead=nullptr. Let the driver guard: if (astPtr->treeHead == nullptr) skip traversal.

nextSteps.name: Alternative: pre-pad semantic stack before each make* call
nextSteps.description: Before every makeBinarySubTree(N) / makeBinarySubTreeWithHead(N) call, check if semanticStackPtr->size() >= N. If not, push (N - size) epsilonNode placeholders to bring it up to N, then proceed normally. No flag needed, no guard needed, works for any deficit regardless of cause. Safest approach.
cons: Silent — doesn't report which node was missing
Could mask bugs in normal parse paths

keyFiles.epsilonNode: src/node.h line 71 — has accept(), safe to use as placeholder

importantConstraints: epsilonNode is the correct placeholder type — it already has accept(visitor&) so visitor dispatch is safe
Do NOT delete popped nodes in error mode — they may still be referenced via sibling/parent pointers
semanticActions has direct access to parsingStack via the parent parser object — no pointer-back needed since skipError is a parser method and semanticHandler is a parser member

The default node() constructor does NOT initialize pointer fields (headOfSibling, leftSibling, rightSibling, parent) to nullptr — only the parameterized constructors do. epsilonNode uses the default constructor.
